question.text: The difference between Gross IRR and Net IRR is:

answer.text: Net IRR is after deducting management fees, carried interest, and expenses; Gross IRR is before these deductions
Net IRR is always higher than Gross IRR

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines gross return metrics as excluding management fees, other fees, expenses and additional returns, while net metrics are more representative of the actual return earned by investors because they include fees and carried interest. Net metrics are typically reported on both pre-tax and post-tax bases. The Trap: Fund managers often highlight Gross IRR to showcase investment skill, but the investor's realised experience is the Net IRR after all fund-level deductions. The workbook's worked example illustrates how the gross-to-net gap is driven by fees, carry, expenses and applicable taxes. Note: The earlier explanation cited a typical 3-5% gross-to-net gap, a 30% gross to 22-25% net translation, a "2-20" fee-structure assumption and 7-10 year fund-life commentary that are not directly supported in the checked workbook pages. Those market-practice numbers have been removed; only the source-backed gross/net definition and pre-tax/post-tax framing are retained.
